study_identification_part.si_4_title: Neurofind: using deep learning to make individualised inferences in brain-based disorders

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The Outlier Detection model uses an adversarial auto-encoder (AAE). The Brain Age model uses support vector regression (SVR), but SVR is not listed in the extraction categories.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: The Outlier Detection model uses an adversarial auto-encoder (AAE), a deep learning approach that has shown promising results in clinical neuroimaging.

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: The study used the volume of 101 regions, including 68 cortical regions (CV), 33 subcortical structures (SubV), ventricles (CSF), and corpus callosum sections (CCMorph).
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: The volume of 101 cortical and subcortical regions was extracted and modelled... The cortical surface was parcellated using the Desikan-Killiany cortical atlas... and segmented into 68 cortical regions... An additional 33 neuroanatomical structures were extracted using the ASEG atlas... totalling 101 brain regions
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Vieira2025.pdf.md: MRI data acquisition and pre-processing

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age and Sex were used as conditional variables in the AAE model.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: To further account for the effect of demographics variables, age and sex were added to the model such that the AAE was conditioned to learn a latent representation whilst taking into account this information.
